description_full: Qualys, Inc. provides cloud-based platform delivering information technology (IT), security, and compliance solutions in the United States and internationally. The company provides Qualys Cloud Apps, which include cybersecurity asset management; enterprise TruRisk management; vulnerability management, detection, and response; total application security; patch management; custom assessment and remediation; multi-vector endpoint detection and response; policy audit; and file integrity monitoring. It offers TotalCloud, a cloud-native application protection platform, which include cloud workload protection, cloud detection and response, cloud security posture management, infrastructure as code, SaaS security posture management, cloud infrastructure and entitlement management, and Kubernetes and container security. In addition, the company markets and sells IT, security, and compliance solutions; offers Qualys' Enterprise TruRisk platform that enables customers to identify and manage IT and operational technology assets; collect and analyze IT security data; discover and prioritize vulnerabilities; quantify cyber risk exposure; recommend and implement remediation actions; and verify the implementation of such actions. Further, it offers asset tagging and management; reporting and dashboards; questionnaires and collaboration; remediation and workflow; big data correlation and analytics engine; and alerts and notifications. The company offers its solutions to enterprises, government entities, and small and medium-sized businesses in various industries, including education, financial services, government, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, media, retail, technology, and utilities through its sales teams, as well as through security consulting organizations, managed service providers, resellers, cloud providers, and consulting firms. Qualys, Inc. was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Foster City, California.

financial_summary: Qualys, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.0B market cap on $669M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +15% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 80% against a 10% cost of capital — a 70-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 78% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $304M in free cash flow — roughly 45 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.56× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 12% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 26pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.42x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+1.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 38% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 12% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 27% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 58% and a beta of 1.12, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $138.3M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 28% in the 2020 crash and 32% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades only 8% below its DCF fair value of $188, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 33%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $134 to $266 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/FCF 19.8 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 33% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 5.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 18 covering analysts target $197 on average, 14% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 80% clears the cost of capital of 10.1% by 70pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.45).
It runs a 78% gross margin and converts 45% of revenue into free cash flow, or 34% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.56x.
ROE of 35% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 9pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 17.5% of revenue on R&D and 11.5% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $250.3M (4% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 8.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.0% over 3 years, 13.0% over 5 years and 15.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 13% of profits supports about 10.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 15.2% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.12 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 77% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 5%.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (0.7% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (47 sales, net $3.2M sold).
It returns 2.9% a year to shareholders (2.9% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 2.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 12.0% of the float, 4.0 days to cover.
people: With about 2,738 employees, each generates about $244K of revenue, 0.7x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 16.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $111K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.3M (6x revenue per employee).
